correctness.rationale: For independent standard exponentials E,E prime and 1<p<2 define Z_s=s(E-1)-(1-s)(E prime-1), s=1/2+t. Let S=E+E prime,D=E-E prime, so Z=D/2+t(S-2), joint (S,D) density e^{-S}/2 on S>0 and |D|<S. The weak second derivative of |u|^p is p(p-1)|u|^{p-2}, locally integrable precisely because p>1. For the d-integrated kernel the rearrangement bound of the translated singular integral by C_p S^{p-1}(S-2)^2 supplies an integrable outer majorant. Thus M_p(0)=2^{-p}Gamma(p+1), M_p prime(0)=0, M_p doubleprime(0)=2^{2-p} Gamma(p+1)(p^2-3p+4). Consequently log ||Z||p has Hessian 4(p^2-3p+4)/p. Variance E[Z^2]=1/2+2t^2 gives logarithmic L2 Hessian 4. Difference is 4(2-p)^2/p>0, proving strict local minimality for each p in (1,2). This is local within the two-sided exponential reduction; there is no claim of global minimization or transition location.
residual_risks: Does not solve global constrained minimization, determine transition p, or exclude additional nonsymmetric minima.
